q: I consumed so much packing list content while I was pregnant in an effort to feel more in control of things so I thought I'd share what I packed and, of that, what I used or didn't use.
cx: Ten days after birth, she says she binged packing-list content in pregnancy to feel in control.

q: MY OWN PILLOW - probably the best thing I brought
cx: Best item in her hospital bag after a six-day stay.

q: Stroller fan: I was SO HOT for the tail end of the induction and the \~2 days after labor. I strapped this fan to my bed and basically kept it running for 3 days.
cx: A stroller fan was one of her most-used hospital-bag items.

q: Laptop and HDMI cord - we used this setup to watch movies on the TV in our room. If you're planning an induction, I think this is a really nice thing to have because it helps so much to pass the time.
cx: For a long induction, a laptop to watch films helped pass the hours.

q:
What I brought and didn't use/really need

* A robe: I spent my whole time either in PJs or just straight up naked when I was very hot
* My iPad - expected to watch movies on it but we also brought the laptop and that was way better for movie-watching
* String lights and flameless candles
cx: Her list of hospital-bag items she never used, including string lights and candles.

q: My husband brought a camping pad to put on top of the foldout couch thing they had for him and he said it helped a lot
cx: Her husband's own packing win for a long hospital stay.

q: I felt really down when I failed the initial screening, so I thought I’d post just in case I could encourage someone else who might feeling like I did!
cx: After failing a first screening test and passing the follow-up, she posts to reassure others.

q: However, whenever I shared my preference with others I felt judged and was constantly questioned. Why would you want to do that? Just give natural birth a go, you can do it, I did it! Don’t do that, it’s major surgery and the recovery will be awful. Every time I’d hear these words I’d just want to cry because it felt like I was crazy even considering it.
cx: UK mother who wanted a planned caesarean recalls what people said whenever she mentioned it.
r: medical: elective c-section; anxiety context; loss mentioned in a reply

q: Might I add that most people with this opinion have never had a planned c-section themselves. These opinions swayed my decision
cx: She notes the critics of her caesarean preference mostly hadn't had one.
r: medical: elective c-section; loss mentioned in a reply

q: I’m an incredibly anxious person, especially surrounding anything medical. As birth came closer and closer, I started to feel incredibly scared and worried about how I would deliver my little one.
cx: Three weeks postpartum, recalling her growing fear as birth approached.

q: I spent many hours researching and everyone’s needs are different. I just could have done with someone telling me to ignore that outside noise!
cx: After hours of research, what she most needed was permission to ignore others' opinions.

q: One of the hardest nights of my recovery was night 1 with baby because she was absolutely ravenous bless her! […] So I was up for 48 hours whilst feeding her and was absolutely exhausted! In the end my husband suggested we get some formula as we always planned on doing combi feeding anyway and that finally settled her
cx: First night after her caesarean she was awake 48 hours feeding until her husband suggested formula.

q: Throughout my pregnancy, I imagined an unmedicated birth in a labor room where I could utilize a shower, bath TENS unit, hypnobirthing… all of the things. We also were working with a doula.
cx: First-time mother, 32, on the birth she planned with a doula and hypnobirthing.

q: So not exactly the calm unmedicated birth I imagined, but that’s ok! Having flexibility and being ok with your preferences changing is, in my mind, the best thing you can do to prepare for your birth.
cx: A week after a fast birth unlike her plan, she calls flexibility the best preparation.

q: She was helpful as being an extra support person for me and my husband, and helped apply counter pressure to my back before the epidural which really got me through. She also took a ton of amazing pictures and videos that we otherwise would not have gotten. […] Unfortunately, we didn’t get to use the pain management/ aromatherapy techniques as we planned, but I’m still happy to have had her throughout pregnancy and the birth itself.
cx: Asked if her doula was worth it after such a fast birth, she lists what the doula actually did.

q: I needed to read only positive ones when I was pregnant.
cx: Agreeing with a commenter that she only read positive birth stories while pregnant.

q: Labor and delivery is the hardest thing I’ve ever done, but I cannot tell you how much it was worth it. Everything about you is open afterwards, your body, your heart, your soul.
cx: Days after her first birth, how it felt.
r: unit: medical condition and a passing mention of stillbirth risk in a reply

q: There was also this good drink called pineapple protein that my Nurse midwife gave me and honestly it saved me.
cx: What kept her going during labour, answering a pregnant commenter.
r: unit: medical condition and a passing mention of stillbirth risk in a reply

q: This was my fourth pregnancy. […] My entire pregnancy I was under the impression that I would be giving birth vaginally. I took vitamins, ate dates, drank strong raspberry tea, bounced on the yoga ball , bought the birthing gown, tens machine, wooden comb, you name it.
cx: In her fourth pregnancy she bought and tried everything to prepare for a vaginal birth; it ended in a caesarean.
r: unit: unwanted c-section, NICU stay, stillbirth named as a doctor's warning

q: I used this entire pregnancy to research and I wasn't strong enough to leave the hospital and wait.
cx: After research all pregnancy, she felt pressured into a caesarean at 38 weeks.
r: unit: unwanted c-section, NICU stay, stillbirth named as a doctor's warning

q: I didn't leave the hospital until 6 days later. A normal---C-section recovery/stay is four days. I was away from my home and hubby and other kids for entire week.
cx: Her six-day hospital stay kept her apart from her husband and other children.
r: unit: unwanted c-section, NICU stay, stillbirth named as a doctor's warning

q: I see a lot of posts here about what methods actually work to speed along a natural labor
cx: Past due, she tried many home methods to start labour, wanting to avoid induction.

q: I’d also been eating a few dates each day, walking a ton, and had sex the day before. I was really trying to get things moving lol (wanted to avoid an induction).
cx: Her list of what she tried at 40+3 to avoid an induction.

q: I was deeply depressed when I found out I was having a boy. It wasn’t what I imagined so realizing reality wasn’t going to match fantasy felt devastating. Part of it was that I felt like I didn’t know how to relate to a boy and any bit of confidence I had in myself as a parent was gone.
cx: Looking back, the reveal of a boy hit her hard in pregnancy.

q: I took baths for hours at a time, with my husband having to actually get in the tub with me to hold and console me.
cx: How her husband comforted her during weeks of gender disappointment.
